title: Noetherian affine minimal-prime charts at fibre component generic points
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $t\in S$, and put $T=X_t$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $C\subseteq T$ be an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] and $y$ a generic point of $C$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Then $T$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Moreover there exists an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq T$ of $y$ such that, with $A=\mathcal O_T(U)$ and $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the ring $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and the prime ideal $\mathfrak p_y\subset A$ corresponding to $y$ under this identification is minimal: no prime ideal of $A$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p_y$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), applied to the fibre over the residue field; Algebra Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), closure and minimal-prime description in an affine chart.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(t)$. Every ideal of the field $k$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$: a nonzero element of an ideal is invertible and hence forces $1$ into the ideal. Thus every ideal is finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$ covers itself and has section ring $k$; hence $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian), applied to the one-chart cover of the spectrum of a field.

proof.text: By the definition of the fibre, $T=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to this projection and the locally Noetherian base from step 1. It follows that $T$ is locally Noetherian. No Noetherianity hypothesis on $S$ is used.

Choose a member $U$ of the Noetherian affine open cover of $T$ containing $y$. By [pqf-def-locnoeth], $A=\mathcal O_T(U)$ is Noetherian. Write $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ using affineness. Taking global sections gives $A\cong B$, because the section ring of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $B$; applying the contravariant spectrum functor gives $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$. Denote by $\mathfrak p_y$ the prime corresponding to $y$.

source.place: Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian), the affine cover in the definition; the spectrum convention of def-weil-affine-spectrum.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p_y$ be any prime of $A$, and let $z\in U$ correspond to it. The affine closure formula [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] gives $y\in\overline{\{z\}}^{\,U}$, hence $y\in D:=\overline{\{z\}}^{\,T}$. Since $D$ is closed, it contains $\overline{\{y\}}^{\,T}=C$. The set $D$ is irreducible: it is nonempty, and if it is covered by two subsets closed in $D$, those subsets are closed in $T$ since $D$ is closed; whichever contains $z$ contains its closure $D$. Maximality of the irreducible component $C$ therefore gives $D=C$. In particular $z\in C\cap U=\overline{\{y\}}^{\,U}$. Here the subspace closure identity follows directly because, for a subset $E\subseteq U$, the closed subsets of $U$ containing $E$ are the intersections with $U$ of closed subsets of $T$ containing $E$. Applying the same affine closure formula now gives $\mathfrak p_y\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Thus $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p_y$, proving minimality.

source.place: Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), part (1), combined with the definitions of generic point and irreducible component (Topology Tags 004X and 004V); the singleton-closure argument is written out.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01T4 and 01T6, followed by the affine closure formula of Algebra Tag 00ES; elementary maximality and subspace-closure argument written explicitly.

Tested on: empty fibre (vacuous); Spec k[e]/e^2, where p_y=(e) is minimal; k[x,y]/(xy), where (x) and (y) are both minimal; an infinite disjoint union of finite-type affines (only local Noetherianity is claimed); a non-Noetherian base S. Steps: (1) a field is Noetherian and Spec k is covered by one chart, which meets pqf-def-locnoeth. (2) def-pc-scheme-fibre gives T=X x_S Spec k(t); lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change (Stacks 01T4, arbitrary base change) and pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft (01T6) then give T locally Noetherian, with nothing assumed about S. (3) Pick a member of the Noetherian affine cover containing y; global sections identify U with Spec A. (4) For a prime q inside p_y at the point z, the affine closure formula (00ES(1), node lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes) gives y in the closure of z. That closure is irreducible and contains C, so it equals C by maximality. The written subspace-closure identity then puts z in the closure of y in U, so p_y lies in q. The inclusion directions are correct and no reducedness or integrality is used. Every cited statement was read and says what its step takes from it.
